title: ALIAS: Evaluating Performance and Memorization in LLM-Written TLA+ Specifications
abstract: arXiv:2610.29767v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memorization inflates the benchmark scores of large language models (LLMs), since a model can reproduce answers it saw in training. Researchers test for it with consistent identifier renaming (CIR), which gives every identifier in a task a new name, and treat a lower score on the renamed task as evidence of recall. We test this method on the Temporal Logic of Actions Plus (TLA+) language, whose model checker acts as an oracle by confirming whether a renamed task preserves the exact behaviors of the original. Across 111 TLA+-Bench tasks, renaming lowers the correctness of Claude Opus 4.8 from 28% to 18% and of GPT-5 from 9% to 7%. Most of this decrease comes from how the test grades, which requires exact names that most descriptions never state. Grading by behavior shrinks the decrease to about 3 percentage points for Opus 4.8 and to 0 for GPT-5. In two model families fine-tuned on disjoint halves of the tasks, renaming removes about half

translated_title: ALIAS：评估大语言模型编写的TLA+规约的性能与记忆化现象
translated_abstract: 记忆化（memorization）会夸大大语言模型（LLM）的基准测试分数，因为模型可以复现其在训练中见过的答案。研究人员通过“一致标识符重命名”（CIR）来检验这种现象，即给任务中的每个标识符起新名字，并将重命名任务上较低的得分视为模型记忆的证据。我们在时序动作逻辑语言（TLA+）上测试了这一方法，该语言的模型检查器可以作为一个“神谕”（oracle），确认重命名后的任务是否保留了原始任务的精确行为。在111个TLA+-Bench任务上，重命名使Claude Opus 4.8的正确率从28%降至18%，GPT-5从9%降至7%。这一下降大部分源于测试的评分方式，即要求提供大多数描述中从未给出的精确名称。若按行为进行评分，下降幅度可缩小至Opus 4.8约3个百分点，GPT-5则为0。在分别在互不相交的任务半区上微调的两个模型家族中，重命名消除了大约一半（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文利用TLA+模型检查器作为验证神谕，发现LLM在标识符重命名任务上的正确率下降主要来自要求精确标识符名称的评分方式，若按行为语义评分，记忆化效应实际很小甚至消失。
en_tdlr: Using TLA+'s model checker as an oracle, ALIAS shows that apparent LLM memorization under consistent identifier renaming largely stems from grading that demands exact identifier names, shrinking to ~3 percentage points or zero when scoring by behavior instead.
